answer: Each additional ongoing medical condition (per-patient count of MHONGO=='Yes') is associated with a ~19.6% increase in the odds of higher COVID-19 severity (per-patient maximum AEHS, 0–7 scale), holding BCG vaccination status and the patient-interaction variables (work_hours, patients_seen, expect_interact) constant: proportional-odds β = 0.1787 (95% CI −0.078 to 0.435), OR = 1.196 (95% CI 0.93–1.54), p = 0.172; i.e. +19.56% (95% CI −7.5% to +54.5%) per additional ongoing condition. The effect is positive and of plausible magnitude but not statistically significant at α=0.05 in the primary per-patient model; sensitivity analyses (per-event: +26.1%, 95% CI 0.2–58.8%, p=0.048; collapsed 4-level outcome: +17.7%) give a consistent, slightly larger positive reading, and the all-1000-patient model (non-COVID coded 0) gives +28.5% (95% CI 12.7–46.5%, p=0.0002) but conflates infection risk with severity and is not the primary basis.
